play.definition: A zone stretch run where the quarterback reads the unblocked edge defender to decide to hand off to the running back or keep the ball, stretching the defense horizontally to create cutback lanes.

action.label: Ball Carry
action.definition: Any action by an offensive player who has possession of the football and is attempting to advance it downfield, including running, scrambling after a reception, or after a fumble recovery.

action.label: Ball Snap
action.definition: The action of the center (or occasionally another player) legally putting the ball into play by handing or tossing it between their legs to a backfield player (typically the quarterback) to initiate a down.

action.label: Block Second Level
action.definition: An offensive player engaging a defender who is past the initial line of scrimmage, typically a linebacker or safety, to create a running lane or protect the passer. This block occurs after the first wave of defensive linemen.

action.label: Keep
action.definition: A quarterback's decision to retain possession of the football after a read-option or run-pass option (RPO) play, choosing to run the ball themselves rather than handing it off or throwing.

action.label: None
action.definition: A temporal label used when the player is visible but is not performing any defined football action in the action taxonomy during the annotated interval.

action.label: Pre Snap
action.definition: The period before the snap when players are set in formation and no active play has begun.

action.label: Read Edge Defender
action.definition: A specific type of 'Read Defender' action, typically performed by a quarterback, where they observe the defensive end or outside linebacker on the edge to decide whether to hand off, keep the ball for a run, or pull the ball back for a pass/option play.

action.label: Snap Receive
action.definition: The action of the quarterback securing the ball from the center’s snap to initiate the play.

action.label: Zone Block
action.definition: An offensive lineman's block in a zone blocking scheme, where linemen are responsible for an area or 'zone' rather than a specific defender. They work in combination with adjacent linemen to create movement and open running lanes, often double-teaming and then releasing to the second level.
